benchmark.category: a single-file open-world college-campus browser game with daily missions, drivable vehicles and a first-person eye view
benchmark.users: students playing on a desktop browser or a phone who run the daily missions, drive around campus and judge how the night drives look

requirements.source_phrase: Show side-quest checkpoints, chai targets and stickers in Eye view so every quest is playable
requirements.statement: In Eye view (CAM.mode=3) on the campus with a side quest active, a cyan waypoint column stands at that quest's current target position in the world for each side quest the player can start (chai, yulu, puffs, rival, tiffin, lost), and the column moves when the target changes
requirements.notes: First clause of the user's Eye View Markers line; the agent's earlier report lists 'Eye view doesn't show side-quest checkpoints' as an open item, so this is unverified. Reach a quest with a giver press (GIVERS[i].x/y then E) or via page.evaluate on the side-quest state per the continuity note.

requirements.source_phrase: Show side-quest checkpoints, chai targets and stickers in Eye view so every quest is playable
requirements.statement: The Eye view marker pass reads the live side-quest target (UI.sideWp) every frame and draws the cyan column at that world position, draws none when no side quest is active, and raises no error for any of the six side-quest kinds
requirements.notes: files_of_reference: EYE VIEW block in /app/frontend/public/game/index.html (fppBuild markers meshes, fppRender 'side quests'). The pass must key on live state, not on a snapshot taken when Eye view was entered.

requirements.source_phrase: Show side-quest checkpoints, chai targets and stickers in Eye view so every quest is playable
requirements.statement: During the chai side quest in Eye view, a floating cyan dot sits above every customer still waiting for chai, and that customer's dot disappears the moment their chai is delivered
requirements.notes: 'chai targets' from the user's line. The count must match the waiting customers exactly at zero and at the start of the quest, not only at the first delivery.

requirements.source_phrase: Show side-quest checkpoints, chai targets and stickers in Eye view so every quest is playable
requirements.statement: The Eye view pass draws one cyan dot above each chai customer whose delivery is still pending, reads that pending list live each frame, and draws no dot once the last customer is served
requirements.notes: A dot list built once at quest start leaves dots over served customers for the rest of the ride.

requirements.source_phrase: Show side-quest checkpoints, chai targets and stickers in Eye view so every quest is playable
requirements.statement: In Eye view each uncollected sticker floats and spins on the ground at its world position in its own colour and disappears from the ground as soon as the player walks into it and collects it
requirements.notes: 'stickers' from the user's line; the agent's earlier report lists collectible stickers as missing from Eye view. Collect one sticker in Eye view and confirm it is gone there and in the 2D view.

requirements.source_phrase: Show side-quest checkpoints, chai targets and stickers in Eye view so every quest is playable
requirements.statement: The Eye view pass draws every ACT.stickers entry whose got flag is false at its world position in that sticker's own colour with a spin, and stops drawing an entry the same frame its got flag becomes true
requirements.notes: Check the drawn set against ACT.stickers before and after a collection; a pass that draws a fixed list leaves ghost stickers after collection.

requirements.source_phrase: Bring wet-road streaks and every car's headlights into Eye view for rainy night drives
requirements.statement: In Eye view on a rainy night (EV.cur='rain', EV.k=1, game clock after 18:00) wet-road streaks run along the road in front of and behind moving vehicles and street-lamp light smears across the road toward the viewer
requirements.notes: First half of the user's Eye View Night Glow line; the agent reported wet-road streaks as missing from Eye view, so this is unverified. Set S.t=1265 and EV.cur='rain' / EV.k=1 through page.evaluate and screenshot from the driver's seat.

requirements.source_phrase: Bring wet-road streaks and every car's headlights into Eye view for rainy night drives
requirements.statement: The Eye view render draws the wet-road streak and lamp-smear layer keyed on the live rain state (EV.cur, EV.k) and the night factor, positioned from each lamp's and vehicle's world coordinates and heading every frame
requirements.notes: files_of_reference: fppRender 'lamps, beams and wet-road streaks'. Keying the layer on a flag captured at load would leave it out entirely on a rainy drive started later.

requirements.source_phrase: Bring wet-road streaks and every car's headlights into Eye view for rainy night drives
requirements.statement: In Eye view at night every moving vehicle other than the player's — traffic cars, autos, bikes and campus buggies — shows a front lamp and a red tail lamp that glow as it moves, so other cars' headlights are visible from the driver's seat
requirements.notes: 'every car's headlights' from the user's line; the agent's earlier report says only the player's own headlight lights the road in Eye view, so the other-vehicle half is the unverified part. Watch a traffic car pass the parked player at S.t=1265.

requirements.source_phrase: Bring wet-road streaks and every car's headlights into Eye view for rainy night drives
requirements.statement: The Eye view night pass draws a front lamp and a red tail lamp on every moving traffic entry and on campus buggies, from each vehicle's position and heading, and draws none for a parked vehicle
requirements.notes: Separate draw branches exist for the player's vehicle and for traffic; a pass that lights only the player's car passes a shallow look and fails this.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: While driving any vehicle in Eye view, a dashboard (#dash) shows a speed gauge and a km/h readout (dash-speed) that follow that vehicle's current speed, reading zero when the vehicle is stopped and rising as it accelerates
requirements.notes: The Dashboard View line; the agent says the dashboard exists, so the testable half is that the gauge follows the vehicle rather than sitting at a fixed value.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The dashboard's speed value is recomputed each frame from the driven vehicle's live speed through the same conversion the 2D speedo uses, rounded to a whole km/h, and shows zero when that speed is zero
requirements.notes: A dashboard fed from a speed captured on entry reads a stale number for the whole drive; compare dash-speed with the vehicle's speed value at rest, mid-drive and at full speed.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The Eye view dashboard's radio display (dash-song) shows the song and artist actually playing while the radio is on, 'Tuning…' while a song is still loading, and 'Radio off' when the radio is off
requirements.notes: The radio-display half of the user's line; the three states are named by the build description and each must be distinguishable on screen.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The dashboard radio text is built from the radio's own state (the playing track's metadata while playing, a tuning state while a track loads, an off state when RADIO is off), so the text equals the track the audio element is playing
requirements.notes: A hard-coded string or a string written only at radio start keeps naming the previous track after a song changes.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The dashboard's Next song button (dash-next-song) skips to a different party song while the radio is on, and is disabled and visibly inactive while the radio is off
requirements.notes: The control half of the dashboard; pressing it must change the song and the display, and its disabled state must look different from its enabled state.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The dashboard's Next button calls the same skip path the R key uses (radioOn's skip function / radioStep), so after a press the playing track changes and the dashboard text and toast name the new track, and the handler does nothing while RADIO.on is false
requirements.notes: Two skip paths that diverge are the realistic bug; compare the track after an R press with the track after a button press.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: While the Eye view dashboard is shown the normal 2D speedo panel and the floating radio pill are hidden, and the dashboard disappears when the player gets out of the vehicle or leaves Eye view
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of the dashboard line: two speedometers and two radio displays on screen is the failure, as is a dashboard left over the walking view.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The dashboard is shown only when the vehicle drives and CAM.mode is Eye view, and that same condition hides the normal speedo panel and the floating radio pill, so leaving the vehicle, leaving Eye view or entering an interior clears the dashboard class
requirements.notes: files_of_reference: fppFrame fppdrive class and #dash markup near #btnRadio. Test the get-out path, the pause-menu camera switch and an interior entry, not only the initial drive.

requirements.source_phrase: Keep the radio and campus music working when a song stalls or fails to load
requirements.statement: When a radio song stalls or errors while the player is driving, the radio moves on to another party song and keeps playing, or if it cannot it turns off and the campus music returns at its normal level, so the ride is never left with both the radio and the campus music silent
requirements.notes: The Radio Safety Net line. The agent's open item 'a song that stalls while loading can leave both the radio and the campus music silent' is the bug this promise rules out. Force a stall and an error on RADIO.el through page.evaluate and listen for campus music after it.

requirements.source_phrase: Keep the radio and campus music working when a song stalls or fails to load
requirements.statement: On an audio error or a stall, radioStep advances to another party track and keeps RADIO playing, and when no further track can play it sets RADIO.on false and musTarget back to the normal campus music level, so at least one of the radio or the campus music is audible at all times
requirements.notes: files_of_reference: CAR RADIO block (radioOn with skipFn/tries/bad, radioStep stall skip, musTarget). A path that sets RADIO.on false without restoring musTarget is the silent-ride bug.

requirements.statement: With no side quest active, Eye view shows no waypoint column, no chai dot and no leftover marker from the previous quest, the scene rendering as it does without the marker layer
requirements.notes: Empty state for the new marker layer: a marker that lingers after its quest ends points the player at nothing.

requirements.statement: The Eye view marker pass draws nothing when the side-quest state is idle, clears the previous quest's column and dots on the frame the quest ends, and raises no error with no quest active
requirements.notes: Complete a side quest inside Eye view and check the marker layer is empty on the next frame.

requirements.statement: A sticker collected in Eye view stays collected: after leaving Eye view, reloading the page and entering Eye view again it is not on the ground and is still counted as held
requirements.notes: Persistence half of the sticker clause; a collection that lives only in the Eye view scene graph vanishes on reload.

requirements.statement: Collecting a sticker writes its got flag through the same state the save stores, and a reload reads that flag back so the marker pass excludes it
requirements.notes: Compare the stored sticker flags before and after a reload; an in-memory-only collect passes a shallow screen check.

requirements.statement: In Eye view at game clock 10:00 (S.t=600) with no rain, no street-lamp smear, wet-road streak, vehicle glow or night tint is drawn, so the daytime 3D scene looks as it did before this pass
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of 'for rainy night drives': a layer drawn unconditionally washes out the day scene. Compare the same camera at S.t=600 and S.t=1265.

requirements.statement: The Eye view glow layers are gated on the night factor being above zero and on the rain state, so at S.t=600 they draw nothing and no error is raised
requirements.notes: A night factor that never reaches zero fades the day scene instead of switching cleanly.

requirements.statement: During the Yulu side quest in Eye view the next gate shows as a bright upright cyan ring and the following gate as a dim one, and passing the bright gate advances both markers
requirements.notes: Build description names the two-ring gate marker as part of 'every quest is playable'; a single ring leaves the player with no look-ahead.

requirements.statement: The Eye view marker pass places the bright ring on the quest's current gate and the dim ring on the gate after it from the live gate index, and moves both when that index advances
requirements.notes: Read the ring positions against the gate list before and after one gate is passed.

requirements.statement: In Eye view every side-quest giver appears as a person with a cyan dot above them, so a quest can be found and started from the 3D view without switching back to the 2D camera
requirements.notes: Build description: GIVERS entries get a cyan dot so the quest can be found from the first-person view; without it 'every quest is playable' in Eye view fails at the start step.

requirements.statement: The Eye view pass draws each GIVERS entry as a person at its world position with a cyan dot above it, and the giver the player is standing next to can be pressed with E to start its side quest while in Eye view
requirements.notes: Both halves matter: a visible giver whose E press does nothing in Eye view still blocks the quest.

requirements.statement: At 1920x800, at 390x844 and at 844x390 with is_mobile+has_touch the Eye view dashboard overlaps no HUD control, mission card or touch button, and its speed value, radio text and Next button are fully visible and readable
requirements.notes: Layout class for the new panel; the sideways-phone HUD is already tight and the dashboard is the newly added box.

requirements.statement: The dashboard's CSS keeps it inside the viewport and outside the computed bounding boxes of the minimap, mission card, stick, SLAP, E and RUN controls at 1920x800, 390x844 and 844x390, and the page reports no horizontal overflow at those widths
requirements.notes: Measure the bounding boxes with a mission running so the mission card is present.

requirements.statement: The dashboard's 'Tuning…', playing and 'Radio off' states look different from each other, and the Next button looks and behaves differently when disabled than when enabled
requirements.notes: UI-state class: three states that render identically leave the player unable to tell loading from off.

requirements.statement: The dashboard's rendered state is derived each frame from the radio's state and the disabled attribute follows RADIO.on, so loading, playing and off render distinct classes and the disabled Next button fires no skip
requirements.notes: A disabled-looking button that still calls the skip handler is the failure a state class alone hides.

requirements.statement: A radio song that never starts playing within about 7 s is skipped to another party track, RADIO.playing becomes true when a later track plays, and the campus music stays ducked only once that track is audible
requirements.notes: From the Radio Safety Net line plus the agent's open item about a stall leaving both the radio and the campus music silent. Simulate with a track that never fires playing; assert the second track plays.

requirements.statement: After three failed tracks in a row the radio turns off, RADIO.on is false, the dashboard shows 'Radio off', and the campus music is restored to its normal level for the rest of the ride
requirements.notes: Terminating case of the safety net: without it every failed track retries forever and the dashboard claims a radio that is not playing.

requirements.statement: The campus music is ducked only while the radio is actually audible (RADIO.playing true), so a song that fails before it starts leaves musTarget at the normal campus level
requirements.notes: Ducking on radio start rather than on first audible sample is the mechanism that produces the silent ride the user's line forbids.

requirements.statement: A radio load error does not mark the shared SONGS entry bad, so the same song still plays from The Terrace's playlist and the radio's own later attempts are not blocked by a stale bad flag
requirements.notes: The agent's open item says a brief radio error removes that song from The Terrace's playlist until a reload; this rules that shared-array mutation out.

requirements.statement: After a failed or skipped song the on-screen radio message names the song actually playing, not the failed one, and does not claim 'Radio on' over silence
requirements.notes: Every action answers on screen truthfully; a toast naming the dead track is the visible half of the radio failure.

requirements.statement: The radio toast and the dashboard text are written from the track that is playing at that moment, after a skip or a failover, and are not written when the new track fails to start
requirements.notes: Compare the toast string with the audio element's current src after forcing an error and a skip.

requirements.statement: The dashboard's km/h value is the driven vehicle's speed multiplied by one conversion constant and rounded to a whole number, so at the same instant it equals the 2D speedo's number for that speed and both are zero at rest
requirements.notes: Class-1 business rule: two speed readouts on two surfaces must agree. Constant and whole-number rounding recorded as the assumption; the test compares the two rendered numbers for the same vehicle state.

requirements.statement: The cyan waypoint column, the chai dots and the dashboard's speed and radio text meet at least 4.5:1 contrast against what is immediately behind them, on a night drive and on a daytime drive
requirements.notes: Layout and visual class for the new overlays; thin cyan over a wet night road is the likely failure.

requirements.statement: The declared colours and opacities for the marker layer and the dashboard panel compute to at least 4.5:1 against the scene tint and panel background they composite over, at day and night
requirements.notes: Compute from the declared values when the pixel sample over the software-rendered canvas is unreliable.

requirements.statement: The Eye view marker and glow layers reuse sprites built once rather than allocating a canvas or gradient per frame, and after entering and leaving Eye view ten times exactly one game loop and one key/touch handler set remain, with no duplicate marker or light objects accumulating
requirements.notes: Resource-leak class. Frame rate itself is not asserted: the continuity note says headless WebGL is software-rendered and very low FPS is expected and must not be reported.

requirements.statement: Entering and leaving a vehicle five times and switching Eye view on and off five times leaves the dashboard, the normal speedo and the radio pill each rendered exactly once, with no stacked duplicate panels
requirements.notes: Repeated show/hide is where a class toggled on show but cleared on a different path accumulates duplicates.

requirements.statement: The dashboard, speedo and radio pill visibility are each driven by one boolean read each frame from the drive and camera state, so repeated enter/leave cycles cannot leave the panels both shown or both hidden
requirements.notes: Read each element's computed display after each cycle rather than counting DOM nodes.

requirements.statement: GET /game/index.html returns 200 containing the EYE VIEW block (marker build and the lamps, beams, wet-road, side-quest and dashboard render paths) and the CAR RADIO block (radioOn with skip and retry accounting, radioStep stall skip), and entering Eye view, driving with the radio and forcing a song error raises no uncaught JS error and no failed request for a game or music asset
requirements.notes: Build and deployment class: one static file behind the preview host, so code that never reached the served copy, or a music path that 404s, is the realistic gap between the agent's report and the product.

requirements.statement: The dashboard's speed gauge shows a needle or arc whose sweep is proportional to the current speed, resting at zero when the vehicle is stopped and moving smoothly as it accelerates
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- a speedometer is a gauge, not a number alone; players read acceleration from the sweep.

requirements.statement: The gauge's needle angle or arc fill is computed from the same speed value the km/h readout shows, mapped across the gauge's full range, so the sweep and the number never disagree
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- a needle wired to a different value than the readout is worse than no needle.

requirements.statement: While a mission is running, the mission's destination marker is visible in Eye view from the driver's seat, so the player can drive toward the objective without switching back to the 2D camera
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- the objective is always findable from behind the wheel; the build already marks missions with gold columns in Eye view and this keeps them live during a mission.

requirements.statement: The Eye view marker pass draws the current mission's destination marker from the live mission target position while a mission runs and removes it when the mission ends
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- a destination column keyed to a stale target sends the player to the wrong place after a mission step changes.

requirements.statement: On a 390x844 touch phone driving in Eye view the dashboard is visible and its Next song button is tappable while the stick, SLAP, E and RUN controls stay usable, and a tap changes the song
requirements.notes: benchmark: browser driving games are judged on a phone -- a dashboard that covers the touch controls, or a Next button no thumb can reach, fails the phone judge.

requirements.statement: The dashboard and its Next button are laid out by the same touch-layout rules that place the stick and action buttons, take the tap on the touch path, and call the same skip function as the R key with no desktop-only branch
requirements.notes: benchmark: browser driving games -- desktop/touch parity, checked by tapping Next with is_mobile+has_touch and comparing the resulting track with an R press.
